title: Body Language & Non-Verbal Communications Skills
overview: Communication is shaped not only by words, but also by posture, facial expression, eye behavior, gestures, voice, interpersonal distance, movement, appearance, timing, and the interaction between these signals. Developing non-verbal communication skills helps professionals become more observant, communicate with greater consistency, and understand how their behavior may be perceived by others.

This course provides an in-depth and practical exploration of body language and non-verbal communication in professional interactions. Participants will learn how to observe behavior systematically, recognize clusters of signals, establish behavioral baselines, distinguish observation from interpretation, and avoid common errors such as judging a person from a single gesture or assuming that one signal has a universal meaning.

The program also develops participants' ability to manage their own non-verbal presence in meetings, presentations, interviews, negotiations, leadership conversations, customer interactions, and difficult discussions. Particular attention is given to facial expressions, gestures, posture, voice, personal space, rapport, confidence, discomfort, engagement, and congruence between verbal and non-verbal messages.

Through observation exercises, video-based analysis, role plays, simulations, and feedback, participants will build a disciplined approach to reading behavioral cues while respecting context, individual differences, and cultural influences.
audience: Managers, supervisors, team leaders, sales and customer-service professionals, HR personnel, interviewers, negotiators, trainers, presenters, public-facing employees, administrative professionals, and anyone whose role requires effective interpersonal communication, observation, influence, relationship building, or interpretation of behavioral cues.
methodology: The course uses an experiential methodology combining short presentations, guided observation, video and image analysis, behavioral-baseline exercises, role plays, paired activities, communication simulations, presentation practice, interview and meeting scenarios, self-observation, peer feedback, and structured reflection. Participants will repeatedly practice separating observable behavior from assumptions and will apply non-verbal communication techniques to realistic professional situations.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the major channels and functions of non-verbal communication.
Observe body language systematically without immediately converting observations into assumptions.
Establish a behavioral baseline and identify meaningful changes from that baseline.
Interpret gestures, posture, facial behavior, eye behavior, voice, distance, and movement within context.
Recognize the importance of clusters, timing, congruence, and situational factors when interpreting behavior.
Identify common interpretation errors and avoid unreliable body-language myths.
Use non-verbal behavior to project confidence, openness, professionalism, and attentiveness.
Build rapport through appropriate non-verbal alignment and responsive communication.
Apply non-verbal observation skills during meetings, interviews, presentations, negotiations, and difficult conversations.
Adapt non-verbal communication to cultural and individual differences.
Develop greater awareness and control of their own non-verbal communication.
